name: stroke-styles
title: Stroke caps, joins and widths
summary: A stroke reference sheet: butt, round and square caps against end guides, widths 2, 8 and 16, and miter, round and bevel joins on stroked rectangles.
prompt: A reference sheet of stroke styles: butt, round and square line caps, stroke widths 2, 8 and 16, and miter, round and bevel corner joins.
teaches: Choose how a stroke ends with strokeCap butt, round or square
Choose how stroke corners meet with strokeJoin miter, round or bevel
Change only one paint property by sending a paint command with just that key; the others carry over
Draw faint guide lines with the paint alpha key
Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre
pitfalls: Paint state persists: the stroke width, cap and style set for one shape apply to every later shape until changed (the join squares reuse the 16 dp width)
alpha scales the current colour; a later color resets it to that colour's own alpha, so the teal lines are opaque again
A square or round cap extends the line by half its width past the endpoint, a butt cap stops exactly on it; the guides at x=90 and x=190 show it
Joins only show on corners of one path or rect: two separate drawLine calls meeting at a point are not joined
drawTextAnchored panX -1 puts the text to the right of x, panX 1 to its left

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: literal coordinates sit in the top-left and get cut off when it is resized, so scale the drawing to fit (or derive positions from componentWidth()/componentHeight())

snippets.note: a 16 dp stroke with strokeCap butt
switch only the cap: paint {strokeCap: round}
strokeJoin miter on a stroked rect: sharp corners
a left-aligned label: panX -1 anchors the text's left edge at x

check.describe: The butt line stops at the guides, round and square overshoot them; widths grow 2/8/16; the three squares have sharp, rounded and cut outer corners. Resized, the whole drawing scales uniformly to fit and stays centred (smaller in a narrow box, centred with margins in a wide one).
